newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire, paper firms sign forestry pact.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire, paper firms sign forestry pact.

text.p: New Hampshire, four major forestry companies and an environmental group signed a trend-setting agreement for harvesting timber from privately owned lands, timberland owners said.
The agreement covers more than 33,000 acres of forest at an elevation above 2,700 feet in the northern region of the state.
The agreement covers about 95 percent of the private land above that elevation, said Eric Kingsley, executive director of the New Hampshire Timberland Owners Association.
The 12-page ageement outlines specific provisions that address road-building, regeneration, residual stand densities, erosion control and harvesting methods.

"It's a non-regulatory approach to ecosystem management. The landowners and the state of New Hampshire...looked at a way where private interest and public values can be protected," Kingsley told Reuters.
Signatories of the agreement include Boise Cascade Corp, Champion International Corp, Crown Vantage Inc, International Paper Co and Hancock Timber Resource Group.
Champion owns about 16,000 of the 33,000 acres covered under the agreement. Boise owns 8,500 acres, Hancock Timber owns 1,600 acres and International Paper owns 1,330 acres.
The Appalachian Trail runs through the private lands and the Appalachian Mountain Club helped draft and negotiate the pact.
